questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

These girls speak English fluently.

options.text: English is spoken fluently by these girls.
English was spoken fluently by these girls.
English has been spoken fluently by these girls.

• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + infinitive + Object (Active voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + to be + past participle + Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The grocer sells fresh vegetables. (Active voice)*
 
• *Fresh vegetables are sold by the grocer. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is ‘these girls’.
 
• The object of the given sentence is ‘English’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• speak will be changed to is spoken.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

“I will help you,” he will say to me.

options.text: He says to me that he would help me.
He will tell me that he will help me.
He tells me that he helped me.
He told me that he will help me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and the task is to convert it into indirect speech.
 
• The phrase "I will help you" becomes "he will help me" in indirect speech - keeping the future form 'will', changing the first person 'I' to third person 'he' and second person 'you' to first person 'me'.
 
• Also, the reporting verb 'say' changes to 'tell'.
 
• Therefore, we have: "He will tell me that he will help me."

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Options 1 ("He says to me that he would help me.") and 4 ("He told me that he will help me.") do not correctly convert direct speech into indirect form.
 
• Option 3 ("He tells me that he helped me.") has the incorrect tense, using the past tense 'helped' instead of future 'will help'.

questions.question:
**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.**

I spend a lot of my time at work helping my customers find an best outfit.

options.text: my time at work helping my

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **customers find an best outfit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in the article used before '**best outfit**'.
 
• It should be '**the**' instead of '**an**'.
 
• We use "**an**" before words that begin with vowel sounds.
 
 
• **For example-** *an apple, an elephant, an hour.*
 
 
 
• We use "**a**" before words that begin with consonant sounds.
 
 
• **For example-** *a cat, a dog, a house.*
 
 
 
• "**The**" is a definite article. It is used to specify a particular noun, making it clear which specific thing or group is being referred to.
 
 
• **For example-** *He is the tallest person in the room.*
 
 
 
• The word "**best**" is in the superlative degree. The superlative degree is used to describe the highest or most extreme level of quality among a group of things.
 
• In this context, "**the best**" indicates a specific category of outfit, the outfit that is the most suitable or appropriate.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**, which contains the error.

**The correct sentence should be:** *I spend a lot of my time at work helping my customers find the best outfit.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: (**No error**) is incorrect as there is an error in the sentence.
 
• Option 2: (**I spend a lot of**) is not the error as it is a part of the correct sentence.
 
• Option 3: (**my time at work helping my**) is not the error as it is a part of the correct sentence.

 The above sentence is in **simple past tense **and the sentence formation for it is - **Subject + Verb + ed (wanted) / verb in the past tense + the rest of the sentence.**
